name: @davidkim9/pixel-art-mcp

tools.name: configure_project
tools.description: Set project settings (all optional): pixelsPerUnit (16), outputDir ("./assets", relative to the project root), defaultPaletteId, atlasPadding (2), atlasExtrude (1), metadataMode ("sidecar" | "embedded" | "both"), importRoots (extra directories assets may be read from), characterExport ("atlas" | "parts"). Returns the full settings.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a document with one layer and one frame. kind: sprite | character | tileset | effect | icon. Uses the default palette unless paletteId is given. Character documents get one layer per part and one frame per direction (parts/directions optional). Warns if the size is not a multiple of 8.

parts.description: character only: part layer names (default head, body, hand_l, hand_r, foot_l, foot_r)

directions.description: character only: directions (default down, up, left, right)

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Ids, names, kinds and sizes of all open documents.

tools.name: get_document_info
tools.description: Layers, frames (durations, tags, labels, pivots), tags, rig / tileset / icon config, symmetry, wrap mode, selection and import source of a document.

tools.name: duplicate_document
tools.description: Deep copy of a document under a new name.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Close a document (removes it from memory and from the next save_project).

tools.name: resize_canvas
tools.description: Resize the canvas of all layers and frames. anchor: top-left, top, top-center, top-right, left, center-left, center, right, center-right, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-center, bottom-right. Pivots and rig points move with the content.

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change to a document (up to 30 steps per document).

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Persist settings, palettes and all documents to outputDir/.pixelmcp/project.json (native JSON format).

tools.name: load_project
tools.description: Load a saved project from outputDir/.pixelmcp/ (or from `dir`), replacing the documents and palettes in memory.

dir.description: Output directory (or its .pixelmcp folder) to load from; default: current outputDir

tools.name: load_palette
tools.description: Load a palette. source: a list of hex colors; the text of a Lospec .hex or GIMP .gpl file; a path to a .png, .aseprite, .gpl or .hex file (inside the project or importRoots); or "builtin:pico8". Index 0 is inserted as transparent, so the first color becomes index 1 (indexed PNG/Aseprite palettes whose entry 0 is transparent keep their indices). Reloading a name replaces that palette. The first palette loaded becomes the project default.

tools.name: list_palettes
tools.description: All loaded palettes with color counts and ramp names.

tools.name: get_palette
tools.description: Colors (index-aligned; index 0 = transparent) and ramps of a palette.

tools.name: render_palette
tools.description: Swatch image of a palette, labelled with indices, plus one row per ramp (dark → light).

tools.name: define_ramp
tools.description: Name a shading ramp: palette indices ordered dark → light. Used by shade_with_ramp, radial_gradient and selective outlines.

tools.name: remap_palette
tools.description: Index-to-index remap over every layer and frame, e.g. {"12": 30, "13": 31}, to make color variants (enemy recolors, team colors, an ice fireball). With newDocName the result is written to a new document and the original is untouched.

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: add_layer
tools.description: Add a layer (on top unless index is given; 0 = bottom). blend "additive" marks a glow layer, exported separately as name_glow.png.

tools.name: remove_layer
tools.description: Delete a layer and its pixels in every frame.

tools.name: rename_layer
tools.description: Change a layer's display name (its id stays the same).

tools.name: reorder_layer
tools.description: Move a layer to newIndex in the stack (0 = bottom).

tools.name: set_layer_visibility
tools.description: Show or hide a layer. Hidden layers are never exported.

tools.name: duplicate_layer
tools.description: Copy a layer (all frames) directly above the original.

tools.name: set_layer_properties
tools.description: Lock/unlock a layer, change its blend mode, or mark it as a guide layer (shown faintly in previews, never exported).

tools.name: add_frame
tools.description: Add a frame at the end (or at index). copyFrom copies another frame's pixels; durationMs defaults to the copied frame's or 100.

tools.name: remove_frame
tools.description: Delete a frame (all layers).

tools.name: duplicate_frame
tools.description: Copy a frame (pixels, duration, tag) right after itself.

tools.name: move_frame
tools.description: Move a frame from one position to another.

tools.name: set_frame_duration
tools.description: Set the duration of one frame, or of frames frame..to (inclusive).

tools.name: tag_frames
tools.description: Name an animation range ("idle", "walk", "explode"): frames from..to inclusive. Re-tagging moves the tag (it is removed from frames outside the range). An empty tag clears tags in the range. direction: forward | reverse | pingpong | pingpong_reverse.

tools.name: set_pivot
tools.description: Set the pivot (anchor) in canvas pixels for all frames, or for frames frame..to. Coordinates are continuous: (0,0) is the top-left corner, (width/2, height) is bottom-center (feet). Exported as pivotPx in the metadata. Default: center (characters: bottom-center).

tools.name: draw_grid
tools.description: PRIMARY DRAWING TOOL. Paints a block of pixels from text. rows: equal-length strings, top to bottom, starting at (x, y). legend maps single characters to palette indices. "." always means "leave unchanged", "_" means transparent (index 0). Example: {"x":4,"y":2,"legend":{"o":1,"s":13,"h":15},"rows":["_ooo_","osssh","osssh","_ooo_"]}. Symmetry and wrap mode apply.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: read_grid
tools.description: Read pixels back as text rows (one character per pixel, "_" = transparent) plus the legend used. Reads one layer, or the flattened visible layers when layerId is omitted on a multi-layer document. Pass a legend to reuse your own character codes. The returned legend can be fed straight back into draw_grid.

tools.name: set_pixels
tools.description: Set scattered pixels: [{x, y, c}] where c is a palette index. pixelPerfect: true treats the list as an ordered freehand stroke and drops L-corner pixels (like Aseprite's pixel-perfect mode). Symmetry and wrap mode apply.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: draw_line
tools.description: Pixel-perfect 1px Bresenham line (8-connected, no doubled corners) from (x0,y0) to (x1,y1), endpoints included.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: draw_rect
tools.description: Rectangle with top-left (x, y) and size w×h; outline only unless filled.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: draw_ellipse
tools.description: Pixel-perfect ellipse covering pixel centers from cx-rx to cx+rx and cy-ry to cy+ry. Integer center + radius gives odd sizes (cx=8, rx=3 → 7px wide); use .5 values for even sizes (cx=7.5, rx=3.5 → 8px wide).

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: draw_path
tools.description: Stroke through a list of points: straight segments, or a smooth curve that passes through every point (curve: true). 1px strokes are pixel-perfect (no doubled L corners) unless pixelPerfect: false. width/widthEnd taper the stroke along its length, which suits branches, roots, trunks, grass blades, tails and hair strands. Example (a branch thinning toward its tip): {"points":[{"x":12,"y":28},{"x":14,"y":20},{"x":20,"y":14}],"curve":true,"width":3,"widthEnd":1,"c":5}. Symmetry and wrap mode apply.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

widthEnd.description: Stroke diameter at the end (default: width)

brush.description: Brush tip for strokes wider than 1px (default circle)

tools.name: draw_polygon
tools.description: Closed shape through 3+ points (pixel centers): outline only, or filled. curve: true smooths the outline into a spline through every point, which gives organic blobs: leaf clusters, canopy masses, bushes, rocks, clouds, puddles. Irregular point spacing reads more natural than an ellipse. outline paints the edge in a second color over the fill. Symmetry and wrap mode apply.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

outline.description: Edge color drawn over the fill (default: c)

tools.name: spray
tools.description: Airbrush / scatter for organic texture: foliage clumps, broken leafy silhouettes, moss, speckles, sparkles, dirt. Sprays dabs inside a circle (x, y, radius) or along a path (points, optionally curve: true). density ≈ fraction of the area covered (0–1). colors picks randomly per dab (weights optional); size sets the dab diameter. Pass stamp {rows, legend} (draw_grid format) to scatter a small motif such as a leaf cluster instead, randomly flipped unless randomFlip: false. within: "opaque" keeps paint inside existing pixels on this layer (texture a canopy), "transparent" only paints empty pixels (grow a ragged edge). falloff thins dabs toward the rim. The same seed reproduces the same result; the seed used is returned.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

points.description: Spray along this path instead of around (x, y)

falloff.description: Thin out toward the rim (default smooth)

brush.description: Brush tip for strokes wider than 1px (default circle)

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

tools.name: pixel_perfect
tools.description: Remove doubled L-corner pixels from 1px lines already on the layer (Aseprite's pixel-perfect, applied after the fact), e.g. after hand-drawn draw_grid linework. A corner pixel only goes when the line stays connected without it; it takes the background color outside the corner. Filled areas are left alone, but square corners of 1px outlines (rectangles) are rounded too, so limit region or pass c to clean only lines of that index.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

c.description: Only clean lines of this palette index

tools.name: flood_fill
tools.description: Paint bucket at (x, y). contiguous (default true) fills the 4-connected region of the same index (wrapping across edges in wrap mode); false replaces that index everywhere in the layer. With symmetry, mirrored seed points are filled too.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: replace_color
tools.description: Replace every pixel of index `from` with `to`, in a region ({x,y,w,h} or "selection") or the whole layer.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

tools.name: clear
tools.description: Set pixels to transparent (index 0) in a region ({x,y,w,h} or "selection") or the whole layer.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

tools.name: set_symmetry
tools.description: Mirror all subsequent drawing (draw_grid, set_pixels, lines, paths, polygons, rects, ellipses, spray, fills). mode: none | horizontal (mirror left↔right) | vertical (mirror top↔bottom) | both. axis {x?, y?} is the mirror line in canvas coordinates; default is the canvas center (e.g. x=8 on a 16px canvas mirrors pixel 0↔15; x=7.5 mirrors around the center of pixel 7).

tools.name: select_rect
tools.description: Select a rectangle. Selections are per document and are used by move/copy/flip/rotate and by region: "selection".

mode.description: How to combine with the current selection (default replace)

tools.name: select_by_color
tools.description: Magic wand. contiguous: true selects the 4-connected region around (x, y) (index defaults to the color there); contiguous: false selects every pixel of `index` in the layer.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

mode.description: How to combine with the current selection (default replace)

tools.name: select_layer_content
tools.description: Select all non-transparent pixels of a layer in a frame.

mode.description: How to combine with the current selection (default replace)

tools.name: deselect
tools.description: Clear the selection of a document.

tools.name: move_selection
tools.description: Move the selected pixels of a layer by (dx, dy); the selection moves too. Transparent selected pixels don't overwrite the destination. Wraps around edges in wrap mode.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: copy_selection
tools.description: Copy the selected pixels of a layer (or the whole layer if nothing is selected) to the clipboard. cut: true also clears them. The clipboard works across documents.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

tools.name: paste
tools.description: Paste the clipboard with its top-left at (x, y). Transparent clipboard pixels don't overwrite. The pasted pixels become the selection.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: flip_selection
tools.description: Mirror the selected pixels (or the whole layer if nothing is selected) within their bounding box. axis: horizontal (left↔right) | vertical (top↔bottom).

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: rotate_selection_90
tools.description: Rotate the selected pixels (or the whole layer) clockwise by 90° × times around the center of their bounding box. Lossless.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: offset_layer
tools.description: Shift a whole layer by (dx, dy). wrap: true moves pixels leaving one edge to the opposite edge (essential for tiles). allFrames applies it to every frame.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: auto_outline
tools.description: Outline the layer's shapes. mode "outside" (default) paints transparent pixels touching the shape; "inside" recolors the shape's edge pixels. connectivity 4 (default, no diagonal corners) or 8. selective: true uses the next darker ramp color of the adjacent fill instead of the flat color c (falls back to c when the fill is in no ramp or already darkest). allFrames applies it to every frame.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: drop_shadow
tools.description: Write a hard drop shadow of a layer, offset by (dx, dy) (default 1, 1), in color c, to a layer named <layer>_shadow directly below it (created or regenerated). Applies to every frame unless frame is given.

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: shade_with_ramp
tools.description: Basic directional shading of a filled shape using a named ramp (dark → light): flat interiors get a middle step, edges facing the light the lightest, edges facing away the darkest. lightDir: top-left (default) | top | top-right | left | right | bottom-left | bottom | bottom-right. The shape is the non-transparent pixels in region; `targets` limits it to those indices (e.g. keep the outline). rim = bevel width in pixels. A starting point to refine by hand.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: radial_gradient
tools.description: Gradient around (cx, cy) quantized to a ramp: lightest at the center, darkest at `radius` (invert: true for the reverse). dither: none | checker | bayer2 | bayer4 | bayer8 blends neighbouring ramp steps. onlyOpaque: true recolors only existing pixels (block out a silhouette first, then color it). Core tool for glows and explosions.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: dither_region
tools.description: Ordered dithering between two indices over a region ({x,y,w,h}, "selection" or whole canvas). ratio 0 = all c1, 1 = all c2, 0.5 = even mix. pattern: checker | bayer2 | bayer4 | bayer8. onlyOpaque limits it to existing pixels.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

region.description: Rectangle {x,y,w,h}, "selection", or omitted for the whole canvas

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: find_orphan_pixels
tools.description: Report isolated single pixels (no opaque neighbour in 8 directions) — usually noise. Checks one frame, or every frame if frame is omitted.

layerId.description: Layer id (optional when the document has a single drawable layer)

tools.name: render_preview
tools.description: Upscaled image of one frame (nearest neighbor) with checkerboard transparency, pixel grid and coordinate rulers. layers: only show these layer ids. Guide layers are drawn faintly.

tools.name: render_frames
tools.description: Contact sheet of all frames (or one tag's frames) side by side, labelled with index, duration, tag and label. Use it to review motion.

tools.name: render_onion
tools.description: The frame drawn over its neighbours: previous frames tinted red, next frames tinted blue, fading with distance.

loop.description: wrap around at the ends (looping animations)

tools.name: render_tiled
tools.description: A frame repeated repeat×repeat (default 3) to spot seams in tiles and textures.

tools.name: render_in_context
tools.description: Several assets side by side at the same scale, bottom-aligned, to check that sizes and styles match. frames: frame per document (default 0). background: "checker" (default) or a hex color.

tools.name: export_gif
tools.description: Write an animated GIF of all frames (or one tag) for a HUMAN to review, scaled up (default 4×). Returns the file path, not an image. Files go to outputDir/.pixelmcp/previews/.

tools.name: set_wrap_mode
tools.description: When enabled, every drawing tool wraps around the canvas edges (pixels leaving one side enter the opposite side). Use it to draw seamless tiles.

tools.name: check_seams
tools.description: Compare opposite edges of a tile (right↔left, bottom↔top): the pixels that touch when it repeats. Reports pixel pairs whose transparency differs or whose contrast is well above the tile's own pixel-to-pixel contrast, with a verdict, plus a 3×3 tiled preview with flagged pixels outlined.

tools.name: create_transition_set
tools.description: Create a tileset document for terrain transitions. template corner15 (default; dual grid): 16 frames where frame index === corner mask (TL*1 + TR*2 + BR*4 + BL*8, 1 = upper terrain); frame 0 is all-lower (leave empty in overlay mode). blob47: 47 cell-centered tiles (frame i = mask in ascending order). A faint, locked guide layer dots the upper-terrain corners of every frame. overlay (default true): lower-terrain corners are transparent, drawn over a separate base. Draw on layer "tiles".

tools.name: generate_autotile
tools.description: Fill in the remaining tiles of a transition set from hand-drawn source tiles, as a starting point to refine. corner15: sources are masks (frame indices) you drew, e.g. [15, 3, 1, 7]; other tiles are derived with lossless flips/rotations (flips preferred) and diagonals 5/10 are composed from two outer corners unless you drew one. blob47: uses the five source tiles (masks 0, 17, 68, 85, 255) quadrant by quadrant. Existing tiles are kept unless overwrite is true. Lighting direction may need hand fixes after rotations.

sources.description: corner15: masks of hand-drawn tiles (default: every non-empty tile)

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: check_transition_set
tools.description: Verify a transition set: every tile exists, and tiles whose edge on the same side has the same corner pair have identical pixels on that edge (e.g. the right edge of every tile with TR=1,BR=0 must match). Also flags high-contrast seams where tiles repeat. Returns mismatches and a 4×4 contact sheet with mismatched edge pixels outlined.

tools.name: render_terrain_preview
tools.description: Render a sample map with the set. map: rows of characters, one per world cell — "#"/"1" or the upper terrain's first letter (e.g. "g") for upper, "."/"0" or the lower terrain's first letter ("d") for lower; or pass your own legend. corner15 sets render on the dual grid (W×H cells → (W+1)×(H+1) tiles, offset by half a tile). Without a map, a built-in test map with every corner combination (diagonals, 1-cell strips) is used. base: {docId, frame} draws a base tile underneath (useful in overlay mode).

tools.name: export_tileset
tools.description: Export a tileset as one indexed PNG atlas with padding + extrusion and metadata listing each tile's rect and its corner mask or blob mask. corner15 sets use a 4×4 grid in mask order (slot 0 = mask 0, empty in overlay mode) so the frame index equals the mask; blob47 metadata includes a 256-entry maskToFrame table. Validation errors (missing tiles, edge mismatches) block the export.

tools.name: define_rig_part
tools.description: Set a part's pivot (rotation/anchor point, canvas pixels; continuous coordinates), optional parent (e.g. hand_l → body) and attachPoint (where it sits on the parent). With direction, sets an override for that direction only. Parts move with their parent in poses.

parent.description: parent layer id, or null to clear

tools.name: set_draw_order
tools.description: Layer ids back → front for one direction. Far-side limbs go behind the body (e.g. facing right: hand_l, foot_l, body, foot_r, head, hand_r).

tools.name: define_pose
tools.description: Define or replace a named pose ("idle_0", "walk_1"): per-part integer pixel offsets {dx, dy}, optional flipX (around the part's pivot) and hidden. Offsets are relative to the parent (a moved body carries head and hands). Poses are mirrored automatically for directions created by mirror_rig.

tools.name: mirror_rig
tools.description: Generate one direction from another (e.g. left from right): flips every part horizontally, swaps _l/_r layers (hand_l ↔ hand_r), mirrors pivots and attach points, and swaps the draw order's left/right parts. Adds the direction (and its frame) if it doesn't exist.

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: render_assembled
tools.description: Character assembled from its parts in draw order with a pose applied. direction omitted → all directions side by side. pose may end in "*" (e.g. "walk_*") to render every matching pose as a sequence. showPivots outlines each part's pivot pixel. Reports parts that stop overlapping their parent.

tools.name: export_character
tools.description: Export a character. mode "atlas" (default from project settings): one packed PNG with every part × direction cropped to its pixels; metadata frames carry part, direction, offsetPx (crop position in the canvas) and pivotPx at the part's pivot, plus a character block with parts, parents, attach points, draw orders, mirrors and poses. mode "parts": name_<part>_<direction>.png per part plus one name.json.

tools.name: create_icon_set
tools.description: Create an icon document: size×size, one frame per icon (count), a drawing layer "icon" and a locked guide layer marking the safe area (margin px, default 1) that outline and shadow need. names labels the frames (used by export_icon_atlas).

tools.name: apply_icon_style
tools.description: Apply the same outline and drop shadow to every icon, for consistency. outline: palette index or {color, connectivity 4|8}; shadow: palette index or {color, dx, dy} (default offset 1,1). They are generated on layers style_outline / style_shadow below the art and regenerated each call, so re-run after editing icons. Omit both to re-apply the last style; pass null to remove one.

preview.description: Also return a preview image of the frame after the change

tools.name: export_icon_atlas
tools.description: Export all icons as one indexed PNG atlas (grid, padding + extrusion) with metadata mapping names to frames/rects ("icons": {name: index}). names (in frame order) override the frame labels.

tools.name: inspect_file
tools.description: Report what a PNG or .aseprite file contains without importing it: size, color mode, embedded palette, unique colors, partial alpha, detected upscale, layers / frames / tags / slices (Aseprite), whether pixel-art-mcp metadata (sidecar JSON or tEXt) is present, and an auto-slicing guess. Use it to plan an import.

tools.name: import_png
tools.description: Open a PNG as a document (the file is never modified). slicing: "metadata" (default when pixel-art-mcp metadata exists — lossless: frames, durations, tags, pivots, trims, masks, rigs; extrusion is discarded) | "none" (one frame) | {frameWidth, frameHeight, margin?, spacing?, count?} in source-image pixels | {asepriteJson: path} for Aseprite sheet JSON | "auto" (detect a grid from transparent gutters; refuses and returns a proposal when ambiguous). Exact color mode fails with every off-palette color listed and imports nothing.

path.description: File path, relative to the project root (must be inside the project or importRoots)

name.description: Document name (default: file name / metadata name)

paletteId.description: Palette to map into (default: the project palette)

colorMode.description: exact (default): fail on any off-palette color; nearest: snap (OKLab) and report; extract: build a new palette

alphaThreshold.description: Alpha below this → transparent, at/above → opaque (default 128)

scale.description: Integer upscale factor to undo; "auto" (default) detects it

tools.name: import_aseprite
tools.description: Open an .aseprite/.ase file as a document, preserving layers (and visibility), frames, durations, tags (forward/reverse/ping-pong) and slices (a slice pivot becomes the frame pivot; slices named like rig parts are reported as candidates). Linked cels become copies; tilemap layers are rendered to pixels. Indexed files keep their palette mapping (transparent index remapped to 0). Non-normal blend modes and opacity are flattened with a warning, except addition/lighten → additive. layerGroups: "flatten-names" (default; "arm/upper") or "merge".

path.description: File path, relative to the project root (must be inside the project or importRoots)

name.description: Document name (default: file name / metadata name)

paletteId.description: Palette to map into (default: the project palette)

colorMode.description: exact (default): fail on any off-palette color; nearest: snap (OKLab) and report; extract: build a new palette

alphaThreshold.description: Alpha below this → transparent, at/above → opaque (default 128)

scale.description: Integer upscale factor to undo; "auto" (default) detects it

includeHidden.description: Keep hidden layers (as hidden layers). Default true.

tools.name: export_to_source
tools.description: Re-export an imported document to its original location: PNG sources are overwritten in place with the original layout and metadata regenerated; .aseprite sources get <name>.png + metadata next to them (writing .aseprite is out of scope). Refuses if the source changed since import, unless force: true.

tools.name: export_png
tools.description: Export one frame (default 0) as a single indexed PNG (palette embedded, index 0 transparent) plus metadata, to outputDir/<name>.png. Visible non-guide layers are flattened; additive layers go to <name>_glow.png. Validation errors block the export.

name.description: export name (default: document name); may contain / for subfolders

tools.name: export_spritesheet
tools.description: Export all frames (or one tag) as an indexed PNG sheet + metadata (frame rects, durations, tags, pivots). layout: row | grid | packed (packed trims each frame; offsetPx gives its position in the canvas). padding/extrude default to project settings. Additive layers export as <name>_glow.png with the same layout.

tools.name: export_aseprite
tools.description: Save the document as an indexed .aseprite file at outputDir/<name>.aseprite, for editing in Aseprite. Keeps every layer (visibility, lock, additive → Addition blend, guides as reference layers), frames and durations, tags with direction, the palette (index 0 transparent) and frame pivots (as a "pivot" slice). Rig data is not stored. Validation problems are reported as warnings, not blockers. Overwrites an existing file.

name.description: file name without extension (default: document name); may contain / for subfolders

tools.name: validate_document
tools.description: Run the export checks: palette range and partial alpha (errors), canvas multiple of 8, orphan pixels, frame durations and tag gaps, tile seams, corner15 completeness and edge matching (error), rig overlaps, icon safe area. Errors block export.

instructions:
Pixel art editor for indexed-color assets (sprites, layered characters, seamless tilesets, effects, icons), exported as indexed PNGs with JSON metadata.

Every pixel is a palette index (0 = transparent). Your only view of the canvas is the preview images the tools return, so look often.

Workflow:
- Load or define the palette and ramps first (load_palette, define_ramp); never use colors outside them.
- Block out silhouettes before detail. Check render_preview after every significant change (or pass preview: true to drawing tools).
- Prefer draw_grid for anything detailed; use read_grid before editing existing work.
- Organic shapes (trees, plants, rocks, hair, clouds): tapered curved strokes with draw_path, irregular blobs with draw_polygon (curve: true), texture and ragged edges with spray (stamps, within). 1px strokes are pixel-perfect; pixel_perfect cleans L corners from hand-drawn lines.
- Animation: review with render_frames and render_onion every time frames change.
- Tiles: check render_tiled and check_seams before exporting; transition sets also need check_transition_set and render_terrain_preview.
- Use render_in_context to confirm new assets match the scale and style of existing ones.
- Editing an existing asset: inspect_file first, import with colorMode "exact", then read_grid and render_preview before changing anything. Change only the pixels the edit requires and use export_to_source so the asset keeps its path.
- undo reverts the last change to a document. save_project persists everything.
